source.citation: James W. Putnam, "Two Cases of Writer's Cramp," Journal of Nervous and Mental Disease 22 (1895): 696–699.

reported.label: T. D. F.
reported.familyHistory: Both parents nervous; father a heavy tobacco user from boyhood and drank freely; brothers and sisters all nervous.

complaints: telegraph sending grew weak; dot-initial characters failed while dash-initial ones did not
had to grip the pen hard to keep the hand from scattering; wrist pain and cramp
head pulled to the right and eyes rolled up whenever he wrote, then whenever he watched anyone write
the same cramp with spreading butter or stropping a razor, and at night when he thought of writing
presentation.course: Began telegraphing at 22. Sending failed from 1886; unable to write with the right hand by 1887; the left hand then failed too. Gave up writing and dictation by 1889. Consulted Putnam in 1892.
presentation.priorTreatment: Prolonged rest, various drugs, and several months of electricity, without benefit.

findings: no anaesthesia and no tenderness along the nerve trunks; some tenderness at Erb's point
no hysterical stigmata; conjunctivae and pharynx sensitive; reflexes normal
on writing two letters: rigid right arm, spasm of the left sternocleidomastoid and trapezius turning the head right, eyes rolled up
writing with the left hand produces only slight head turning
eyes examined by an oculist: normal vision and muscle balance
no pain or spasm if he writes while looking out of the window
periodDiagnosis: writer's and telegrapher's cramp, with symptoms judged psychic in nature

treatments.treatment: hypnotic suggestion three times a week for a month
treatments.response: neck spasm eased when writing in the doctor's office, but returned in full away from it

treatments.treatment: galvanism, rhythmic gymnastics, and atropine injections into the neck muscles
treatments.response: some improvement; could sign his name in the office

treatments.treatment: told he would recover in a year if he did not attempt writing until then
treatments.response: kept to it; resumed writing in April 1893 and by 1894 worked eight to ten hours a day without cramp

outcome: Recovered after about two and a half years without writing, followed by a gradual return to work.
quotes: If he looked out of the wiijdow, however, he could write without any pain
so clearly psychic in their nature that suggestive treatment was instituted

modernReading.text: Task-specific focal dystonia (writer's cramp) with cervical involvement. The spread to watching others write and to thinking about writing suggests a large functional component. The long rest and graded return fit the course of either.

fixed: task-triggered cramp of the hand spreading to neck and eyes
relief when not looking at the writing
failure of rest, drugs, and electricity

constrained.rule: work dominated by one repeated fine hand task: telegrapher, clerk, copyist, stenographer, engraver, dentist, compositor
25–55, with at least five years in the trade
comfortable or sponsored; losing the trade means losing the income

notes: The same article's second case (a dentist, Dr. H.) could become its own card.
